audit.why: 52.51% over 2693 games. Xerath owns the ranged lane (Q 750, W 1000, E 1050 against Rake at 650 and Noxian Diplomacy at 575), but Talon's Assassin's Path lets him enter from any wall, so the danger is dive windows and roams rather than the lane trade. The page's HARD 8/10 label is the one thing that does not sit comfortably with the data — flagged as a question, not changed.

audit.whatIsWrong: All seven phases[N].side read 'Talon' while every phases[N].why described Xerath winning that stage, and all seven content win[N] read 'Xerath'. The page rendered two opposite answers for every row.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Xerath on all seven rows, content win[0..6] is Xerath on all seven, and each existing why is written from Xerath's winning side. The full-layer side column was the stale one.
audit.corrected: All seven phases[N].side flipped to Xerath. The whys already match the new verdict, so they were left as written. win[N] already read Xerath, so no content edits were proposed (they would be no-ops and would take the chart group down).
sources: currentText content win[0..6] and full phases[N].why

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns named Rake but carried no numbers, and dosFull[1].d promised 'hold E for the dive' while its body was the tradeGood poke line.
audit.why: Rake (W) is 650 range on 9/8.5/8/7.5/7 and the returning blades carry both the bonus damage and the slow. Noxian Diplomacy (Q) leaps from 575. Assassin's Path (E) itself has effectively no cooldown — it is the piece of terrain that goes on a long one, so he gets exactly one entry per wall. Shocking Orb (E) is 1050 range on 13s at rank 1 and stops him in mid-vault.
audit.corrected: Real ranges and cooldowns written into breakdown.cooldowns; dosFull[1].d regrounded on the 1050/13s stun against the wall-hop.

edits.before: - Talon Rake: matchup-defining — The boomerang return is most of his lane damage — stand off the return line. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget E Shocking Orb for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Rake (W) is 650 range on 9s at rank 1 and the returning blades carry the damage and slow — stand off the return line, step up while it is down. - Noxian Diplomacy (Q) leaps from 575. - Your 13s Shocking Orb is for his commit, never the wave.

edits.before: Q the last-hit from beyond his answer range, W the lateral dodge, and walk — a one-way trade he can only end by leaving the lane.
edits.after: Shocking Orb is 1050 range on 13s and it catches him mid-vault — spend it on the Assassin's Path entry, never on a wave you could clear.

edits.before: Spending E on chip and then watching the dash you bought it for arrive on schedule — the stun is your only 'no' and everyone knows it.
edits.after: From half HP, Rake plus a Q leap plus three Blade's End stacks bleeds the rest out — step back the moment Shocking Orb is not up.

edits.before: Q the last-hit from beyond his answer range, W the lateral dodge, and walk — a one-way trade he can only end by leaving the lane.
edits.after: Q his last-hit from 750 with minions between you, W the sidestep, and walk — he cannot answer that without spending Rake or a wall.

edits.before: Talon wins by landing Rake, denying your pattern, and turning your every misstep into the all-in you hadn’t budgeted.
edits.after: Talon wins by vaulting a wall with Assassin's Path, opening Rake at 650, and bleeding you out before your one 13s stun answers.

edits.before: Carry from the next postal code — no champion converts vision and distance into damage like Xerath; your job is never being where the fight thinks you are.
edits.after: You carry by never standing where a wall-hop reaches: fight from 1050 with both flanks warded, and let Shocking Orb — not your footwork — be the thing that tells Talon no.

edits.before: If Talon opens the score, reset expectations and respect Rake doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm with max-range Qs and stay relevant through R snipes.
edits.after: If Talon opens the score he one-combos you through Doran's — ward both wall entries and farm at max range. After a second, buy the stopwatch and leave tower only for R snipes.

notes: The seven-row side flip is the main fix: full phases[N].side said Talon on every row while the why under each row described Xerath winning, and content win[0..6] plus packet levelChart both said Xerath. Talon's E cooldown reads as 0 in the kit; the real constraint is the per-terrain cooldown, so the page says one entry per wall rather than quoting a number.
